SMTO-HTTP-0028 — SMTO formatted the data for a web request the wrong way

GUID: aa3f6b7f-27df-4060-979f-4ac2c49dee9d
Slug: json-body-appears-serialized
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO packed the data for a web request as a single block of text instead of separate fields, so the service would have misread it. The request was stopped before sending, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue for a moment; SMTO usually fixes the format on its next step by itself. This message tells SMTO exactly what to change, and nothing was sent yet.
  2. If the same message appears again, tell SMTO in the conversation: "Send the request body as an object with fields, not as a quoted text string." A clear instruction stops SMTO from repeating the same wrongly formatted request.
  3. If you really meant to send that text exactly as written, tell SMTO to send it as plain text and set the content type the service expects. Plain text is sent unchanged, so the service receives exactly what you wrote.

What success looks like

  • The request is sent and SMTO shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste passwords or tokens into the request text while trying to fix this; nothing was sent, so no change needs undoing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The http.request json_body was a string that parses as a JSON object or array, indicating it was serialized one layer too early; no HTTP request was sent.

What this means

  • A string supplied as JSON parses into an object or array, showing that a structured container was serialized one layer too early. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A string supplied as JSON parses into an object or array, showing that a structured container was serialized one layer too early.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the body value's type, distinguishing an intentional scalar string from a serialized container.

How to fix it

  • reject_serialized_json_container (gateway_core/http_contract.py) rejects a json_body string that parses to an object or array, since sending it would double-encode the body. Pass the object or array directly as json_body, or use text_body with an explicit Content-Type for intentional raw JSON text.
  • Supply a JSON object or supported body structure instead of a pre-serialized JSON string.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The JSON body carries the intended structure exactly once.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
